delimiter_comma.csv.description: Standard comma-delimited file with no dialect quirks.

delimiter_semicolon.csv.description: Semicolon-delimited file with accented characters (common EU export format).

delimiter_tab.tsv.description: Tab-delimited (TSV) file; extension deliberately still generic to test content-based detection.

delimiter_pipe.csv.description: Pipe-delimited file, common in legacy mainframe/EDI-style exports.

delimiter_inside_quoted_field.csv.description: Comma-delimited file where a quoted field legitimately contains the delimiter character.
delimiter_inside_quoted_field.csv.notes: The model must not mistake the comma inside the quoted field for a fourth column.

encoding_utf8_bom.csv.description: UTF-8 file with a byte-order mark, as produced by Excel's 'CSV UTF-8' export.
encoding_utf8_bom.csv.notes: chardet typically reports this as 'UTF-8-SIG'; the BOM itself must not leak into the first column name.

encoding_latin1.csv.description: Semicolon-delimited file encoded as Latin-1/cp1252, not valid UTF-8 (classic legacy Windows export).
encoding_latin1.csv.notes: These bytes are not valid UTF-8; the agent must not silently mangle accented characters.

encoding_utf16le_bom.csv.description: UTF-16 LE file with BOM, tab-delimited (classic old-Excel 'Unicode Text' export).
encoding_utf16le_bom.csv.notes: A classic 'unexpected file' gotcha: every other byte is 0x00 when misread as a single-byte encoding.

header_metadata_banner.csv.description: Two comment/metadata lines before the real header row (export banner style).

header_none_data_only.csv.description: No header row at all; data starts on the very first line.
header_none_data_only.csv.notes: Ground truth is intentionally null: there is no real header row. The agent should either say so in 'notes' or return a low 'confidence', not confidently assert a fabricated header row.

header_duplicated_mid_file.csv.description: The header row is repeated mid-file, as happens when exports get concatenated.
header_duplicated_mid_file.csv.notes: The duplicated header mid-file is a structural anomaly the agent should flag in 'notes', not treat as a data row.

footer_summary_totals.csv.description: Production-sized ledger (~14 KiB) with a totals row appended after the data, sharing the same delimiter.
footer_summary_totals.csv.notes: Larger than the default head + tail budget, so the footer is only visible in the tail sample.

footer_end_marker.csv.description: Production-sized ledger (~14 KiB) followed by a blank line, an 'end of report' marker and a generation timestamp.
footer_end_marker.csv.notes: Regression case: the timestamp line used to be misclassified as a header/metadata line.

header_and_footer_combined.csv.description: Production-sized semicolon export (~14 KiB) with a two-line banner before the header and a blank line, totals row and end-of-report marker after the data.
header_and_footer_combined.csv.notes: The banner is only visible in the head sample and the footer only in the tail sample.

quoting_doubled_quotes.csv.description: Standard RFC 4180 escaping: an embedded double-quote is doubled ("").

quoting_backslash_escape.csv.description: Backslash-escaped quotes inside fields, as produced by some MySQL/legacy exporters.

quoting_embedded_newline.csv.description: A quoted field spans a real physical newline (a genuinely multi-line CSV record).
quoting_embedded_newline.csv.notes: Byte-prefix/suffix sampling cannot reliably parse multi-line quoted records: a head or tail window may cut this field mid-record. Documented as a known limitation rather than solved by this iteration.

quoting_inconsistent.csv.description: Mixed quoting: some fields quoted, others not, within the same file.

quoting_trailing_empty_field.csv.description: A trailing delimiter leaves an empty last field on some rows.

ragged_rows_inconsistent_columns.csv.description: Rows have an inconsistent number of fields (some trailing values missing).
ragged_rows_inconsistent_columns.csv.notes: Row 2 is missing a field, row 3 has an extra one; the agent should note this rather than error out.

line_endings_mixed_crlf_lf.csv.description: Mixed line endings (\r\n and \n) within the same file, from concatenated cross-OS exports.

no_trailing_newline_eof.csv.description: The last line has no terminating newline character at end of file.

blank_lines_between_rows.csv.description: Stray blank lines interspersed between data rows.

empty_file.csv.description: A completely empty (zero-byte) file — extreme edge case for both head and tail reads.
empty_file.csv.notes: read_sample_bytes and read_tail_bytes must both return b'' without raising; inspect_csv then raises EmptySampleError before invoking any model, since there is nothing to infer from.

header_only_no_data.csv.description: A header row is present but there are zero data rows.

numeric_european_format.csv.notes: 'Importe' should ideally be inferred as a numeric type despite the European formatting, not as a plain string; worth tracking separately as a column-typing quality metric.

null_representations_mixed.csv.description: Inconsistent null markers across rows: empty string, NULL, N/A, '-', NaN.
null_representations_mixed.csv.notes: 'Observaciones' should be flagged nullable=True; the mix of null markers is worth a mention in 'notes'.

whitespace_padded_fields.csv.description: Fields padded with spaces around the delimiter, from a fixed-width-to-CSV conversion.
